name: Chegodi
shortDesc: Crispy Andhra ring murukku — chegodi made from rice flour with sesame and cumin.

image.name: /chegodi-1.jpg
image.alt: Chegodi — crispy Andhra rice flour ring snacks, golden brown

desc: Chegodi (చేగోడీ) is a classic Andhra snack — a crispy, ring-shaped murukku made from rice flour mixed with roasted sesame seeds, cumin, chillies, and butter. Unlike regular murukku which is coiled, chegodi is shaped into individual rings (the name literally means 'ring snack' in Telugu). The rice flour base gives chegodi a lighter, crispier texture than wheat-based snacks, and the sesame seeds add nuttiness. A festival favorite and daily tea-time snack across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — especially popular during Diwali and Ugadi.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 2–3 weeks. Best consumed within 10 days of opening for maximum crispiness.

name: Jantikalu
shortDesc: Crispy Andhra chakli — jantikalu made from rice flour and roasted gram with Guntur chilli.

image.name: /jantikalu-1.jpg
image.alt: Jantikalu — coiled Andhra murukku snack, crispy and golden

desc: Jantikalu (జంతికలు) are the Andhra version of chakli — coiled, spiral-shaped fried snacks made from rice flour and roasted gram flour, seasoned with Guntur red chillies, cumin, and sesame seeds. The word jantika is the Telugu name for the murukku mold used to press these spirals. Jantikalu are slightly denser and more intensely spiced than chegodi, with a satisfying crunch and a clean, spiced finish. A staple homemade festival snack that is now available in small-batch artisan form — made without refined oil or artificial additives.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Shelf life: 2–3 weeks at room temperature. Do not refrigerate — this softens the snack.

name: Challa Mirchi
shortDesc: Andhra buttermilk-marinated dried chillies — fried to a crisp, tangy and fiery.

image.name: /challa-mirchi-1.jpg
image.alt: Challa Mirchi — golden fried buttermilk-marinated dried Andhra chillies on white plate

desc: Challa mirchi (చల్ల మిర్చి — also called majjiga mirchi or mor milagai in South India) is a uniquely Andhra snack preparation: green chillies are slit, soaked in salted buttermilk for 2–3 days, then sun-dried and deep-fried. The buttermilk soak mellows the chilli's raw heat and imparts a pleasant tanginess — the fried result is crispy, salty, sour, and fiery all at once. Traditionally served alongside curd rice or sambar rice as a crunchy accompaniment. A beloved Andhra kitchen staple that transforms simple chillies into a complex condiment-snack.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Shelf life: 1–2 weeks at room temperature. Best eaten fresh from frying.

name: Dahi Mirchi
shortDesc: Yogurt-marinated dried chillies — tangy, slightly sour sun-dried Andhra mirchi.

image.name: /dahi-mirchi-1.jpg
image.alt: Dahi Mirchi — yogurt-marinated sun-dried Andhra chillies, wrinkled and tan-colored

desc: Dahi mirchi is similar to challa mirchi but uses thick curd (dahi/yogurt) instead of buttermilk for the marinade — producing a richer, more intense sour-fermented flavor. Green chillies are slit, packed with salted yogurt, and sun-dried over several days. The yogurt sugars ferment slightly during drying, adding a mild complexity beyond simple acidity. The result is a shriveled, intensely flavored dried chilli with tangy, salty, and spiced notes. Eaten fried as a side with rice and dal, or served as a bold condiment.
storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Shelf life: 1 month (dried form, before frying). Fry before serving.

name: Gumadkai Vadiyalu
shortDesc: Sun-dried Andhra pumpkin papads — gumadkai vadiyalu, crispy when deep-fried.

image.name: /vadiyalu-1.jpg
image.alt: Gumadkai Vadiyalu — sun-dried Andhra pumpkin papad rounds, pale tan color

desc: Gumadkai vadiyalu (pumpkin vadiyalu in English) are sun-dried Andhra papads made from grated ash gourd / pumpkin mixed with rice flour, cumin, chilli, and salt, then shaped into thin rounds and sun-dried for 3–4 days. They are eaten deep-fried or air-fried until they puff up into crispy, translucent rounds. Vadiyalu are a classic Andhra monsoon preparation — made during summer when the sun is strong enough for drying, then stored and consumed through the rest of the year. These are not raw papads — they are pre-dried vadiyalu ready to fry and eat.
storage: Store in an airtight container or ziplock bag. Shelf life: 6 months (dried, before frying). Fry in hot oil until puffed and golden — takes 30 seconds per side.

name: Andhra Boondi Mixture
shortDesc: Spiced Andhra-style boondi mixture — crispy gram flour drops with peanuts and curry leaves.

image.name: /boondi-mixture-1.jpg
image.alt: Andhra Boondi Mixture — crispy golden boondi drops mixed with peanuts and curry leaves

desc: Andhra boondi mixture is a spiced savory snack made from crispy gram flour droplets (boondi) mixed with fried peanuts, curry leaves, dried chillies, and Andhra-style spice seasoning. The Andhra version uses more Guntur red chilli heat compared to North Indian mixtures, giving a characteristic fieriness alongside the crunch. Every batch is freshly made without artificial additives — just gram flour, groundnut oil, and whole spices.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 2–3 weeks. Stays crispiest in the first week.

name: Cornflakes Mixture
shortDesc: Crunchy Andhra-spiced cornflakes mixture with peanuts, dry fruits and Guntur chilli.

image.name: /cornflakes-mixture-1.jpg
image.alt: Andhra Cornflakes Mixture — golden spiced cornflakes with peanuts and dry fruits

desc: Cornflakes mixture is a popular Andhra-style spiced snack mix using puffed corn flakes as the base, tossed with fried peanuts, cashew pieces, curry leaves, raisins, and Andhra spice seasoning. The combination of crispy corn, sweet raisins, and fiery Guntur chilli seasoning creates a snack that hits multiple flavor notes simultaneously. A lighter alternative to traditional fried mixtures with a satisfying crunch.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Shelf life: 2–3 weeks. Best eaten within 1 week of opening.

name: Andhra Roasted Kaju
shortDesc: Andhra-spiced roasted cashews with Guntur chilli and salt — crunchy premium cashews.

image.name: /images/snacks/kaju-roasted-hero.jpg
image.alt: Andhra Roasted Kaju — premium roasted cashews with kaju chikki on clean beige background

desc: Andhra roasted kaju (vejjan jidi pappu in Telugu) are premium whole cashews roasted and seasoned with Guntur red chilli, black pepper, and salt in the Andhra style. The roasting is done in small batches to achieve even color without burning — the result is a deeply golden, crunchy cashew with a satisfying heat that builds as you eat. Cashews are rich in heart-healthy monounsaturated fats, magnesium, and zinc. The Andhra-style seasoning transforms a standard nut into a distinctive snack.
storage: Store in an airtight container away from moisture. Shelf life: 1 month at room temperature, 2 months refrigerated.

name: Ariselu
shortDesc: Traditional Andhra rice sweet with jaggery — ariselu, the Sankranti festival essential.

image.name: /images/sweets/ariselu-hero.jpg
image.alt: Ariselu — traditional Andhra rice and jaggery sweet, golden fried rounds with sesame seeds

desc: Ariselu (అరిసెలు) is one of the most iconic Andhra sweets — a flat, disc-shaped sweet made from soaked and ground rice dough combined with melted jaggery, then deep-fried and coated with poppy seeds or sesame. Ariselu has a distinctive chewy-crispy texture — crispy on the outside from frying, with a soft, jaggery-scented rice interior. This is the sweet that defines Makar Sankranti in Andhra Pradesh — no festival is complete without a plate of fresh ariselu. Made with traditional unrefined jaggery and raw rice — no refined sugar, no artificial flavors.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 1–2 weeks. Best consumed within 5 days for peak texture.

name: Madta Kaja
shortDesc: Kakinada's famous honeycomb sweet — madta kaja with layers of crispy fried dough in sugar syrup.

image.name: /images/sweets/madta-kaja-hero.jpg
image.alt: Madta Kaja — layered spiral Andhra sweet on cream background, golden brown honeycomb interior

desc: Madta Kaja (మడత కాజా) is one of the most celebrated sweets from Andhra Pradesh — originating from Kakinada in East Godavari, the same district our pickles come from. Kaja is made by rolling maida dough into very thin sheets, stacking and folding them into a compact brick, then deep-frying until golden and layered like a honeycomb. The fried kaja is immediately soaked in thick sugar syrup until completely saturated — the result is a crispy exterior that gives way to sweet, syrup-laden layers inside. Kakinada kaja is a GI-tagged (Geographical Indication) product — a protected designation that recognizes its unique heritage.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 1–2 weeks. Best enjoyed within 1 week for optimal crunchiness before the layers soften.

name: Sunundalu
shortDesc: Andhra urad dal laddus — sunundalu, protein-rich traditional sweet with ghee and jaggery.

image.name: /sunundalu-1.jpg
image.alt: Sunundalu — round Andhra urad dal laddus in white bowl, pale cream color

desc: Sunundalu (సున్నుండలు) are traditional Andhra urad dal laddus — made from finely roasted and ground urad dal (black gram) combined with powdered jaggery and pure ghee, shaped into smooth balls. Urad dal is nutritionally exceptional — one of the richest plant sources of protein, iron, folate, and B vitamins. Sunundalu are traditionally made for new mothers post-delivery (as a nutritional recovery food), for festival offerings, and as an everyday sweet. Our sunundalu use unrefined jaggery for natural sweetness and pure cow ghee for binding and flavor.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 2 weeks. Refrigerate for up to 1 month.

name: Pootharekulu
shortDesc: Andhra rice paper rolls with jaggery and dry fruits — pootharekulu from Atreyapuram.

image.name: /pootharekulu-1.jpg
image.alt: Pootharekulu — thin Andhra rice paper rolls with dry fruit filling, laid on dark surface

desc: Pootharekulu (పూతరేకులు — literally 'coating leaf') is a uniquely Andhra sweet and one of the most technically demanding confections in Indian cuisine. Paper-thin sheets of rice starch are made by spreading rice batter on the outside of an earthen pot and quickly peeling off the resulting translucent film. These delicate sheets are then layered with powdered jaggery, ghee, and dry fruits (cashews, almonds, raisins), rolled into cylinders, and sealed with ghee. Pootharekulu from Atreyapuram in East Godavari have GI tag status — they are protected as a heritage food product. Our pootharekulu are made in the traditional Atreyapuram style.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place. Shelf life: 1 week at room temperature, 2 weeks refrigerated. Handle gently — the rice paper sheets are delicate.

name: Rose Cake (Gulab Puvu)
shortDesc: Andhra rose-shaped fried sweet — gulab puvu made from maida batter, crispy and sugared.

image.name: /gulab-puvu-1.jpg
image.alt: Gulab Puvu — rose-shaped Andhra fried sweet, golden and dusted with powdered sugar

desc: Gulab Puvu (గులాబ్ పువ్వు — literally 'rose flower') are delicate, flower-shaped fried sweets made using a specialized rose cake mold (called the 'achchu' mold). Maida batter is dipped onto the heated metal rose mold, then submerged in hot oil — the batter clings to the mold and fries into a perfectly crispy rose shape. The fried rose cake is dusted with powdered sugar and cardamom for serving. Gulab puvu are a popular Andhra fair food, festival sweet, and home celebration treat — their striking appearance and light, airy crunch make them unlike any other fried sweet. Made without artificial colors.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Best consumed within 3–5 days. Do not refrigerate — humidity softens the delicate structure.

name: Bellam Gavalu
shortDesc: Andhra jaggery shell sweets — bellam gavalu, crispy fried dough coated in jaggery syrup.

image.name: /bellam-gavalu-1.jpg
image.alt: Bellam Gavalu — shell-shaped Andhra fried sweets coated in dark jaggery, piled in bowl

desc: Bellam Gavalu (బెల్లం గవ్వలు — 'jaggery shells') are a traditional Andhra festival sweet made by shaping maida dough into small shell shapes using a special comb or ridged board to create the characteristic ribbed pattern, then deep-frying until golden and coating in thick jaggery syrup. The jaggery coating sets into a crispy, caramel-like shell that contrasts with the crunchy fried interior. Bellam gavalu are a Sankranti special — traditionally made alongside ariselu and sunundalu for the harvest festival. The unrefined jaggery coating gives a depth of flavor (molasses, caramel, earthiness) that refined sugar cannot replicate.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 2 weeks. The jaggery coating will stay crispy in a dry environment.

name: Kaju Chikki
shortDesc: Cashew brittle in jaggery — kaju chikki with whole cashews and unrefined jaggery.

image.name: /images/sweets/kaju-chikki-hero.jpg
image.alt: Kaju Chikki — glossy caramelized cashew brittle on white background, premium pieces

desc: Kaju chikki is a cashew brittle made from whole or roughly broken cashews set in a jaggery syrup that is cooked to the hard-crack stage, then poured thin and cooled into slabs. Our chikki uses unrefined jaggery (not refined sugar) for a more complex, molasses-forward sweetness that complements the buttery cashew flavor better than white sugar. The result is a glossy, amber-colored brittle with satisfying crunch and a clean, pure cashew and jaggery flavor. No artificial flavors, no glucose syrup — just cashews, jaggery, and a touch of ghee.
storage: Store in an airtight container away from humidity. Shelf life: 3 weeks at room temperature. Heat or humidity will soften the brittle.

name: Boondi Laddu
shortDesc: Classic boondi laddu with gram flour drops, sugar syrup, cardamom and cashews.

image.name: /images/sweets/boondi-laddu-hero.jpg
image.alt: Boondi Laddu — rich saffron yellow laddus with cashew garnish on clean light background

desc: Boondi laddu (boondi undalu in Telugu) are made by frying small droplets of gram flour batter in ghee until golden, then soaking them in spiced sugar syrup and binding them into round balls while still warm. Cardamom, saffron, cashews, and raisins are mixed in for flavor and texture. Our boondi laddus are made with pure ghee — not refined oil — giving them the authentic richness and aroma that machine-made laddus cannot replicate. A prasad staple in Andhra temples and a wedding sweet tradition.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 1 week. Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

name: Milk Mysore Pak
shortDesc: Soft, melt-in-mouth gram flour sweet with pure ghee — milk mysore pak style.

image.name: /images/sweets/mysore-pak-hero.jpg
image.alt: Milk Mysore Pak — soft golden gram flour ghee sweet pieces on white background

desc: Milk Mysore Pak is a softer, more fudge-like variation of the classic Mysore Pak — using milk alongside ghee and gram flour to achieve a pale, smooth, melt-in-mouth texture different from the traditional crumbly Mysore Pak. The gram flour is cooked in an abundance of ghee over a slow flame until it reaches a thick, glossy stage, then poured into trays and cooled into soft squares. The result is intensely rich, buttery, and aromatic with cardamom — one of the most indulgent Indian sweets. Made with pure cow ghee.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Shelf life: 1 week at room temperature, 2 weeks refrigerated. Bring to room temperature before serving for best texture.

name: Dry Fruits Laddu
shortDesc: Nutrient-dense laddus packed with dates, cashews, almonds, walnuts and jaggery — no sugar.

image.name: /dry-fruits-laddu-1.jpg
image.alt: Dry Fruits Laddu — dark brown laddus packed with dates and mixed nuts

desc: Dry Fruits Laddu is a no-refined-sugar sweet made by binding together a mixture of dates, cashews, almonds, walnuts, pistachios, and raisins with ghee and cardamom — with jaggery as the only sweetener. No maida, no refined sugar, no glucose. These are dense, nutritious laddus that provide sustained energy from natural fats and fruit sugars. Popular as a post-workout snack, a pregnancy/post-delivery nutritional sweet, and a guilt-free festival alternative. Each laddu is packed with iron, magnesium, calcium, and healthy fats.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Refrigerate in summer months. Shelf life: 2 weeks at room temperature, 1 month refrigerated.

name: Rava Laddu
shortDesc: Classic semolina laddus with ghee, cashews and cardamom — rava undalu.

image.name: /rava-laddu-1.jpg
image.alt: Rava Laddu — golden semolina laddus with cashew garnish, warm ghee aroma

desc: Rava laddu (rava undalu in Telugu, sooji laddu in Hindi) are round sweets made from roasted semolina (rava/sooji) cooked with sugar, ghee, cardamom, and dry fruits. The roasted semolina gives a characteristic grainy texture that is distinctly different from smooth besan or urad laddus — each bite has a pleasant sandy-sweet crunch. Cashews and raisins are embedded throughout for richness. Rava laddus are one of the easiest homemade Indian sweets and one of the most universally loved — found in every state, celebrated at every festival.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature. Shelf life: 10 days. Refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.

name: Gond Katira Laddu
shortDesc: Edible gum laddus with dry fruits and ghee — warming, strengthening post-winter sweet.

image.name: /gond-laddu-1.jpg
image.alt: Gond Katira Laddu — dark brown edible gum laddu with dry fruits, dense and warming

desc: Gond Katira Laddu (also called gondh laddu) are made with edible gum (gond katira / tragacanth gum) fried in ghee until puffed, then ground and mixed with whole wheat flour, roasted nuts, dried coconut, jaggery, and abundant ghee. Gond has been used in Ayurvedic nutrition for centuries as a bone-strengthening, back-pain-relieving, and body-warming food — traditionally given to new mothers and consumed in winter. These laddus are dense, calorie-rich, and deeply warming — not an everyday sweet but a medicinal confection with long heritage.
storage: Store in an airtight container. Shelf life: 2–3 weeks at room temperature. Best eaten during winter months when the body can utilize the warming properties.
